chapters.html:
Mydei knows that look on Castorice’s face.

“No,” he refuses firmly. He’s become more accustomed to dishing out rejections since moving to Okhema. It’s a necessary skill to survive life with Phainon, after all. 

Mydei, let’s go to the baths! Mydei, spar with me! Mydei, I'm craving some of your honeycakes!

His requests are endless and his pursuit for Mydei’s attention at every hour of every day is persistent. If Mydei squints hard enough, he thinks he would be able to make out a fluffy tail wagging behind Phainon’s back as he drags him by the arm into another pointless side quest.

It isn't that he hates the attention. Mydei’s real frustration lies in the fact that Phainon only seeks to tease him and push his buttons for his own amusement, and as he throws his head back into a melodic, hearty laugh at his annoyed face, Phainon misses the ever-present yearning in Mydei’s eyes and the way he allows Phainon to continue clinging to him even as he huffs dramatically. 

Simply put, Mydei would be a lot less inclined to reject these invitations if Phainon’s desires aligned with his. 

Just as he’s losing himself in his thoughts (as he always does when it comes to that damn deliverer), the corners of Castorice’s lips turn up to form a devious smile and jolt him back to his horrifying reality.

“Why not? It would boost our sales and make everyone very happy,” she insists, holding the questionable pile of pink and white ruffles up as close as she can to his face. 

Forget physical touch, Mydei is convinced the demigod of death is capable of murder with just a few words. 

The Chrysos Heirs have gathered at Aedes Elysiae at Cyrene’s insistence to assist in running a restaurant for the fairies residing at the Membrance Maze. Mydei had been doing quite for himself as the restaurant’s head chef, but of course Castorice had to come up with the brilliant idea of hosting a special one-day event where the patrons could be served by a cute maid. 

And who is more suited to play the role of said maid than…. Mydeimos the Undying?

He twists his arm to hover over that one spot in his lower back, almost like a nervous tick, and avoids meeting the mischief twinkling in her eyes. 

“Does it have to be me, though? This seems like the kind of job for Hyacine, or maybe Cyrene.” 

Or even Phai-

Castorice shakes her head. Titans, she’s impossible once she’s set her mind to something. And unlike a certain someone, she calmly stands her ground instead of making pathetic puppy eyes and begging until she gets her way. “Lord Mydei, do you know what a gap moe is?”

“Is Stelle teaching you weird things again?” The Chrysos Heirs still haven't recovered from the time the Trailblazer introduced Castorice to the Omegaverse. 

“N-no-” She frowns, and Mydei is momentarily pleased that he succeeded at cracking through her defenses. “Well, it did come from Miss Stelle, but it fits you so perfectly that I would have come up with the term eventually! Lord Phainon calls it the Duality of Strife, and I have to say I do enjoy his fondness for dramatics.” 

Mydei visibly perks up at the mention of the name that swirls at the back of his mind every waking moment of his immortal existence. It only lasts for a split second, but the menace returning to Castorice’s normally gentle smile tells him he’s been caught. “And why exactly does that idiot have a say on this subject?” he asks, his tone emulating nonchalance to protect his pride. 

“Hm? Lord Phainon loves to proclaim that he knows everything about you,” Castorice explains matter-of-factly. “The Kremnoan children have taken up to quizzing him about you to prove his worth.”

Prove his worth for what? Mydei wants to ask, before deciding it’s not worth the disappointment because the answer can't possibly be what he has in mind.

“He’s an idiot,” he huffs instead, fondness seeping through his voice. 

Castorice clears her throat. “Anyway, your gap moe, or the contrast between your ehm… intimidating aura and gentle disposition has always been the subject of admiration. Some might even say it’s your charm point!” She clasps her hands together. “Just think about it, the fiercest warrior in Amphoreus in a pretty pink dress. We’d sell out by noon.”

Mydei has always been awkward with praise, so he struggles to figure out what to make of her assessment, and whether it’s even a compliment at all. Is this really how everyone perceives him? 

“I believe my gentle side has been greatly exaggerated for the sake of senseless idolization,” he says. How often does the average Amphoreus citizen get to see the mushy soft core buried underneath his indestructible shell, anyway? Is Phainon also going around running his mouth about how Mydei likes to sleep with stuffed animals? “I merely seek to be a selfless and just ruler to all the people under my custody.”

Castorice’s eyes are glazed over, almost like she’s tuning out his predictable counter points. 

Then, cruelly, she decides to pull the Phainon Special. 

“Please, Lord Mydei,” she pleads, tilting her head to the side.

Mydei is cornered. Castorice is very dear to him, and he’s long resolved to help her make warm memories and experience the happiness she’s been robbed of throughout her years of solitude. 

Even if it means wearing a maid costume. 

“Fine,” he yields, and pure joy lights up her face like a crackle of fireworks. Mydei begins to consider that it might all be worth it.

She unfurls the pile in her hands to reveal the frilly pastel monstrosity in all its glory. 

He can tell from a glance that it’s too short for his towering figure, but the rest of the proportions seem wide enough to contain his sculpted muscles. The pink dress is adorned with a bow over the frankly too low neckline, generous layers of ruffles at the hem, and a white apron that cinched higher at the waist to accentuate the wearer’s chest. Perhaps the scandalous length is intentional…?

“I have one condition,” he hurriedly adds after getting a clearer image of how this thing would wrap around his glorious and hard earned warrior body, and Castorice nods frantically before even hearing it. Wow, she really wants this to happen. “He can’t see me in it.” 

“Who is he?” she asks, feigning ignorance. Nikador’s balls, is she really going to make him say it? 

“Castorice,” Mydei warns in exasperation, and she laughs.

“He said that he can’t join us tomorrow because he accidentally volunteered to become a test subject for some experiments at the Grove.”

That’s just like Phainon. Always getting caught up in trying to fix the problems of everyone around him even at the expense of his own time. Spending the day at the restaurant is nothing compared to the physical strain of training in the barracks, but Mydei is sure that he’s wearing himself thin right now because he got sidetracked at least 50 times trying to relieve the other demigods of the burden of their own responsibilities.

He knows that Phainon considers him his closest friend. They do spend all their time together, and their affection runs deeper than shallow designations like comrade and rival.

He also knows that Phainon is going to bring this up every chance he gets, and Mydei can’t endure any more humiliation. It’s embarrassing enough that he allows the man he’s been hopelessly in love with to drag him around as he pleases, all because he secretly savors every moment that he spends with him.

What if he likes seeing you in the dress, though? A tiny, desperate voice pokes from the back of his mind.

There have been moments where Mydei felt a flicker of hope that his feelings might not be as onesided as he believes. Moments like–

“My dear Mydei! Aren’t you a sight for my sour eyes,” Phainon exclaims as he snakes his arms around Mydei’s bare waist and nuzzles his face deep into his neck. “I worked so hard today, let’s go to the baths.”

This one.

“HKS, stop messing around,” Mydei grumbles, golden blood shooting down to his groin as he feels Phainon’s hot breath brush against his skin. Phainon’s fingers knead soothing circles into his waist. He’s gotten in the habit of massaging him at the end of each day, absently offering acts of service even when he’s on the verge of passing out in the warm embrace of Mydei’s hefty chest.

 (It wouldn’t be the first time.) (The deliverer always leaves a puddle of drool.)

It’s all becoming more difficult to bear with each passing day. Mydei struggles to keep his lewd thoughts at bay when Phainon is pressed against him like this, clingy and persistent. All Mydei can think about is how it would feel to have Phainon whisper in his ear from this same angle, telling him how pretty he looks between the trail of kisses he would press along his neck and jaw as he pounds deep into him. 

His breath hitches in his throat at the mental image. If Phainon caught on to the subtle shift in his demeanor, he doesn't say anything.

How can he do things like this so easily? It’s the casualness of it all that extinguishes Mydei’s fleeting moments of hope. If Phainon’s feelings mirrored the intimacy of his gestures, wouldn’t he be so much more deliberate and purposeful? As his best friend, Mydei feels like he’s been inside Phainon’s head. He knows just how much he overthinks and deliberates every single move he makes, how he’s secretly harboring a massive ball of nerves and anxiety caused by the crushing weight of everyone’s expectations. 

Much like Kephale himself.

“You’ll come with me if I do?”

I would have come with you even if meteors were raining down from the sky. “I’ll consider it once we return to Okhema.”

“Then we better hurry!”

“See you tomorrow, then,” Mydei waves to Castorice, Phainon’s weight slumping against his body momentarily making him forget about the dreadful promise he made to Castorice. 

“I’m looking forward to it,” Castorice nods with a smile.

--------------------------------------------- 

Immortal demigods don't take sick leaves from their job at the fairy restaurant.

Mydei spends the next morning trying and failing to come up with an excuse to back out, but with Castorice’s reassurance that Phainon won't be there to see him, he swallows his pride and makes his way to Aedes Elysiae.

It’s two hours to opening, but Castorice is already there, chatting up a storm with Hyacine and Cyrene. That can't be good.

His sense of dread only multiplies when she gasps and rushes to greet him, and the two other demigods fall silent, donning identical expressions of mischief. 

“Lord Mydei!” she chirps. “We thought we’d come in early to help you with your costume.”

“Must we really turn this into a spectacle?” he grunts, but the sizzle of excitement in the air reaffirms his decision. If it makes everyone really happy, then he’s willing to put up with a little discomfort.

“The word I would use is hm… moral support?” Cyrene corrects. “You are today’s main attraction, after all.”

“You just want to see me in a dress,” Mydei rebukes, and she shrugs without denying his accusation. They haven’t had the chance to truly become acquainted, but Mydei understands why she and Phainon are best friends. 

Before he knows it, he’s being dragged to a supply closet that had been turned into a makeshift dressing room. The girls help him into the dress, taking extra care to neatly tie all the ribbons and decorate his hair with pretty clips and a matching pink headdress.

It’s a perfect fit, clearly made especially for him. “This is a waste of the Goldweaver’s craftsmanship.”

“You would not be saying that if you saw the look on her face when we presented the idea,” Cyrene sing-songs as she ties the back of his apron into a neat bow.

Hyacine digs into her pouch of charms and accessories, burying her hand deep into it until she fishes out a cat hair clip.

“Lord Phainon likes cats,” she says as she delicately attaches it to his blond curls. “Feral, skittish cats.” 

He does a better job hiding his reaction to hearing Phainon’s name this time. “How is this relevant?”

His eyes dart to Castorice, who conveniently has her back to him at that very moment. 

Hyacine doesn't answer the question.

Mydei must be overthinking it. Right? Right.

It’s not as uncomfortable as he thought. It feels a little strange, sure, but a wave of confidence surges in Mydei as he feels the dress squeeze him in all the right places.

He looks cute, and Phainon loves cute things.

“We still have an hour until opening, so how about a test run?” Cyrene suggests, clasping her hands together. 

Mydei is confused. “Are there any significant differences between a maid and a regular server?” 

“Cassie, you should have explained what the role entailed a little bit more,” Hyacine says.

“I'm sorry,” Castorice gasps, her hand flying to her mouth. “I was so happy Lord Mydei agreed to my request that all the details slipped off my mind.” 

She appears to be in genuine distress, prompting Mydei to quickly diffuse the situation. “It's okay, explain everything to me and I'll practice it before opening.”

Fifteen minutes and many failed moe moe kyuns later, Mydei finds himself standing at the restaurant’s front door.

“We have one customer waiting inside,” Cyrene explains. It must be one of the staff fairies. That should be simple enough, Mydei thinks. “Don't think about it too hard and do your best!”

“We're all rooting for you!” Hyacine offers encouragement while making last second adjustments to the bow on his chest. 

He appreciates the support, but finds it almost comical how the girls are acting like he's leaving to fight the black tide all alone. Perhaps they finally recognize just how big of an ask this is.

“Lord Mydei,” Castorice whispers in his ear as he steps inside. “I really hope that you can forgive me.”

Mydei's confusion about her cryptic apology lasts only for a split second, because he instantly makes eye contact with the supposed test subject.

It's Phainon.

“Hi. Uhm. Wow,” he says intelligently. 

Mydei's heart is pumping, and he's ready to turn on his heel and storm off, but Castorice's pleading face, Cyrene's excitement, and Hyacine's efforts to make him look as cute as a Kremnoan warrior possibly could all hold him in place. They worked so hard for this, and he cares about them too much to let them down. Perhaps Castorice made another error in her excitement and forgot to keep Phainon off the premises but was too scared to tell him. 

“You're not who I expected to see here,” Mydei folds his arms and keeps a respectable distance.

I… Nobody told me the maid was going to be you, either,” Phainon splutters, his face resembling professor Anaxa's plump tomatoes. “It really suits you, Mydeimos.”

This idiot. Why does he look so flustered? Is he feeling secondhand embarrassment on Mydei's behalf? That might be an even worse reaction than outright teasing him.

And yet, hearing those words spurs something in his chest. It feels good to receive Phainon's praise, regardless of the context. 

“Castorice said you were going to be at the Grove today.”

“Huh? She told me the professor needed me to help with an experiment he was conducting on the restaurant's crops, but once I got here she said it was actually a study to test the effectiveness of maids or something. I’m beginning to doubt that the professor is involved at all.”

Okay. It's becoming increasingly difficult to believe the purity of her intentions. 

Now that he thinks about it, shouldn’t the three masterminds behind this idea be in the room during this supposed test run?

There are more reasons than not for him to leave and refuse to play his part, but the rational part of Mydei’s brain pushes common sense to the side for a very simple reason.

He gets to be alone with Phainon.

Running the restaurant alongside his friends has been a fun distraction, and he especially enjoyed competing with Phainon in the kitchen, but he would be lying if he said he didn’t miss the spare time they got to spend together away from everyone else, patrolling Okhema’s sleepy streets in the early hours of the morning, sharing Mydei’s homecooked meals at his place every day, and sparring by the outskirts of Castrum Kremnos. All they have now is their nightly baths, and those are becoming less frequent due to their busy schedule. 

The brief, quiet pockets of his daily life where he got to be just Mydei were no longer spent alone, not with Phainon filling that cavity in his heart that he didn’t even know existed. Despite his best efforts, he’s come to rely on that stupid deliverer for emotional support, and living without his constant attention is now quite inconvenient. 

An hour to opening. He’s going to make the most of it.

“Let's just get this over with, or that tiny pink terror won’t let me hear the end of it,” Mydei mutters, and Phainon beams. 

“Cyrene is the one who put you up to this? That’s just like her,” Phainon says fondly, seemingly unconcerned with the implication that she bullied Mydei into putting the dress, and Mydei’s chest twists with a pang of embarrassing, pathetic jealousy. It’s nonsensical because he’s heard her tease Phainon over the sorry state of his love life more than once, but Mydei can never be reasonable when it comes to Phainon. 

“Her, Castorice and Hyacine with some assistance from Aglaea, apparently,” he explains. “Those three proved to be quite the lethal combination.”  

Phainon is resting a hand on his chin, and his blue eyes lock into Mydei’s with an unfamiliar intensity that knocks the breath out of his lungs. His face is still flushed, but there is a new air of confidence and purpose in his demeanor. “I can’t fault them, though, what with you looking like this.” 

Looking like what? What the fuck is he babbling about? 

“Mydei, it's just you and me here. Let go of your anxiety and just play your part to the fullest,” Phainon whispers. It comes out as a plea rather than a reassurance. 

He’s clearly not in the right state of mind, because his best friend would point out how ridiculous he looks in that headdress or how his chest is about to burst out from beneath the comically big bow, and this detachment from reality helps ease Mydei’s nerves just a bit. 

“HKS, stop acting weird.” he spits out. Has he been possessed by Zagreus? The last thing he needs right now is Cipher’s meddling. 

“Oh? I don’t think that’s how a maid addresses a customer,” Phainon counters with a twisted smile, not unlike the ones he has when he’s about to challenge Mydei to a competition on the battlefield. “I believe the right term is… master?”

Phainon is out of his fucking mind.

Mydei is about to cuss him out again and tell him to behave, but Phainon's plea rings loud and clear in his mind. It's just the two of them. There is no one to scrutinize and judge the incredibly stupid decision that he's about to make. He can be selfish and indulge himself just for a moment, can't he?

He plops his ass down on the edge of the wooden table. “What would you like to have, master?”

Phainon fails to maintain eye contact, his gaze darting down just a little lower, and Mydei figures that it's his confidence faltering just a bit. 

He's silent for a moment, and ah, that hamster wheel in his brain must be spinning at the speed of light. The edge of the table digs at Mydei's thighs, and his dress rides up too high and reveals too much of his legs for his liking, but he remains still and lets his best friend gather his thoughts. 

“I'd like it if my maid was just a little sweeter to me,” Phainon says, extending a hand out and letting it hover in the air for what feels like a million years. 

Finally, his coarse fingers curl around Mydei's, giving his hand a gentle and reassuring squeeze.

I'll show you the Kremnoan definition of sweet, Mydei wants to threaten.

Instead, he says: “Sweet, how?” 

“Like, if your words were as pretty as you are right now.”

It should be difficult, impossible to soften his rough outer edges when he's so accustomed to projecting might and strength. But as Mydei peers at the man below him, looking up at him with a mixture of amusement and something he can't pinpoint yet, he lets the waves of affection crash over his reservations, and it all comes to him so easily.

“Master, are you teasing me?” He’s asking as part of whatever game they’re playing right now, but also for himself. He needs to know, and this might be the only way he can get Phainon to confess his intentions. “Because if you are, all I can offer you is the familiar taste of my fists ♡”

Phainon laughs, but it’s not the same carefree airy sound Mydei has grown to love. There is an edge to it. He’s nervous? “I’m not this time, I promise. I want to see that side of you Mydei, even if it’s just for a bit.”

This isn’t a test run. It’s not practice for future customers. It’s something else. Something for the two of them alone. 

“As you wish, Master Phainon,” his voice dips to a whisper. “I’ll fulfill all your desires.”

He expects Phainon to ask for a massage, or an infinite supply of honeycakes, or for Mydei to join him for a bath after work tonight. No matter how silly it is, he’s happy to oblige.

But there is a darkness swirling in Phainon’s eyes, a different sort of hunger, and he hesitates again before making his request.

“There is just one thing I’d like to have.” 

Before Mydei could register the weight of his words, Phainon stands up so they’re at eye level and plants his palms on the table, caging Mydei between his arms  

Deliverer, what the fuck do you think you’re doing? Sane Mydei would growl.

“What is it, master?” This Mydei asks. 

Phainon always looks like the human embodiment of the sun.

But when he’s this close, with unmistakable lust clouding his pretty eyes? 

Mydei thinks he’s breathtaking. 

“Mydeimos,” Phainon gasps, pathetic, desperate.

A possessive hand grasps firmly into his waist, and Mydei can’t bite back the pleased sigh at the contact. 

“Titans, what has gotten into you?” Mydei wonders, giving Phainon one chance to back out. 

“Will you please let me do it?” 

Phainon bumps their foreheads together, his breathing shallow, and a single lick of his lips clears the ambiguity of his intentions. 

Mydei nods, lightheaded and confused as to how this dream can feel so vivid, and Phainon doesn't spare a single second.

Despite the desperation emanating through every pore of his body, Phainon’s plush lips press into Mydei’s gently, like he’s afraid to break him.

It doesn't last long, though, because Mydei deepens the kiss immediately, inhaling sharply to take in his comforting, familiar scent and parting his lips to let Phainon's tongue inside. With an approving growl, Phainon accepts the invitation and sucks on Mydei’s lips with great fervor. 

Once they part, Mydei feels like he’s seeing his best friend for the first time.

He’s not the lovable, cuddly puppy vying for his attention. He’s a wolf sizing his prey, and he’s still shaking like a leaf.

Phainon hadn’t been nervous or flustered seeing Mydei in the dress, he was fighting against every cell in his body to hold himself back from jumping his bones. 

It’s funny, Mydei had always admired this side of Phainon. His fierce enthusiasm and passion for the things he cares about are always on open display.

He never even dared allow himself to hope to be the target of that same passion. 

Right, Mydei might be misunderstanding the current situation. It’s not his everyday self that Phainon kissed senseless just now, and it’s not his everyday self that he's looking at right now with drunken, insatiable eyes. 

“Are you just doing this because you're turned on by my costume?” Mydei asks, because he would rather they never touch at all than to have his deepest desire fulfilled while being just out of his reach at the same time . There is a lot he can endure. But this? He's not sure he would be able to bear it. 

“Because I like you so, so much Mydeimos,” Phainon licks at the side of his jaw, and Mydei melts, relief soothing the anxiety ravaging his heart. “I've wanted you from the moment I first laid my eyes on you.”

“This isn't just a fetish?” he asks again, just to be sure. He wants to hear it again and again and again. 

“Mydei, my fetish and the sole object of my desires is you, bent over in every position you could think of,” Phainon asserts matter-of-factly.

“I’ll crush you between my thighs,” Mydei grumbles, embarrassed. 

“I’ve already set my mind to fuck you, stop trying to seduce me.” Phainon hesitates for a moment. “You would like that too, right?” 

“Took you long enough to notice, deliverer,” he confesses shyly. 

“Too cute.” Phainon’s lips are on him again, sneaking a hand under Mydei’s dress. “I should be allowed to ascend to godhood solely for holding myself back as long as I did.” 

Oh. He wants to do it here. Right now. 

Mydei digs his nails into Phainon’s shoulders and draws three long breaths to pace himself. There is nothing in this world that he would like to do more than rip this stupid uniform off and let Phainon have his way, but he has responsibilities to attend to. 

“If you ruin Hyacine’s hard work she’s going to feed you to that beast,” he warns as he gently pulls himself away.

“Does it matter if I do, though?”

“You might have forgotten, but work starts soon, deliverer,” Mydei says. “And I do have to begin serving customers in this dress.”

Phainon smiles as he goes for another kiss. “I don’t want anyone else to see you like this, though.”

--------------------------------------------- 

one week ago

Phainon is confident that he’s learned more useful information from Stelle than all the classes he attended at the Grove combined. 

“And they have all kinds of establishments in the dreamscape, things you wouldn’t even think about,” she tells him as she scrolls through photographs on her teleslate-like device one evening. They’re gathered with a handful of the other demigods at the Chrysos Heirs bath after a meeting. Much to his chagrin, Mydei chose to leave and spend the rest of the evening with the Kremnoan Detachment. 

Phainon has been most curious about Penacony. Being born into a doomed world with sorrow accompanying him like an old friend, the concept of a planet where he can be anything he wanted without fear or consequences sounds like an impossible, overly indulgent fantasy. 

It would be nice to visit with Mydei, maybe he would finally muster the courage to be upfront about his feelings, maybe they can get married, maybe he can have the Crown Prince all to himself without sharing his time and attention with Mydei’s subjects or his responsibilities as a Chrysos Heir, and maybe he can test both of their staminas to the limit once Phainon finally has Mydei in his bed on their wedding night.

The sweet dream he’s crafting is supplemented by the colorful and foreign visuals in Stelle’s photographs. She’s flipping over each one quickly and mindlessly, showcasing brightly lit street signs, sprawling cityscapes, and luxurious residences, when a particular one catches his eye. 

“What’s this one for, then?” he asks, tapping her arm before she scrolls too far away, and Stelle happily obliges.

He stares at what appears to be a restaurant of some sorts, but with distinct pastel colored decor that stood out from the rest of the other parts of the dream world he’s seen so far, and most importantly, beautiful servers wearing frilly and impractical dresses.

“Ah, we call this a maid cafe. The servers wear these cute uniforms and do a little bit of roleplay with the customers. The food sucked, but it was two hours of cute girls calling me master and pampering me, so I would say it was worth the visit.”

A maid cafe. He pictures Mydei in a dress like this, doting over him and referring to him as his master, blushing profusely when Phainon drags him into his lap and slips his hand under the dress but sighing and gasping happily at every touch. 

“Lord Phainon, has some interesting taste,” Castorice notes with a mysterious smile, leading Hyacine to snort through her nose. 

Cyrene skips over to them to have a look, and hums curiously when she sees the image in question. “Quite the contrast from his real life preferences.” 

Phainon's ears suddenly feel hot. He’ll never get used to everyone talking about his infatuation with the Crown Prince like they're discussing the weather. It’s a miracle they’ve gone this long without letting his secret slip in front of Mydei.

“I’m never talking to you about my love life ever again. And besides…” he takes another look at the picture. His beloved Mydei is just as cute without the costumes or bright colors, with his pretty blond curls, his flushed face when he receives unexpected praise, his round and cushy pecs, and his pure, gentle smile when he’s playing with the children. “I don't think it’s as big of a difference as you seem to believe.”

“It’s hopeless, Renie. He’s too far gone.” Hyacine rolls her eyes. 

“No, no, this is very enlightening. Don't you agree, Cas?”
